name: Nishika Optical N8000
note: the body and box say 'Nishika N8000' and every listing appends '3D'; the record carries the corporate 'Optical' word nobody types.

name: Mamiya 528TL
note: the top plate is engraved 'Mamiya/Sekor', which US sellers reproduce; the record is filed under the bare brand.

name: Mamiya 1000 DTL
note: as above — the US-market DTL bodies were sold under the Mamiya/Sekor name.

name: Mamiya 500 DTL
note: as above.

name: Whitehouse Products Beacon II
note: sellers say 'Whitehouse Beacon II' or just 'Beacon II'; no other maker used the Beacon II designation.

name: Canonflex
note: same 1959 SLR filed with and without the brand word; nothing distinguishes the records but the prefix.

name: Canonflex RM
note: brand-prefix duplicate of the 1962 RM, as above. The prefix-less record carries the meter facts (selenium, metered) and the merge keeps them.

name: Canon Canonflex RM
note: the body is engraved 'CANON RM' and that is what sellers type; 'Canonflex' is the line name of the record.

name: Canon Canonflex
note: the Canonflex line takes the Canon R breech-lock mount (1959-1964, predecessor of FL). The merged-away twin carried 'Canon RF', which is the rangefinder-era screw registry, not this mount.

name: Kodak VR35 K400
note: the VR35 line name is dropped in most listings; K-numbers are unique within Kodak.

name: Kodak VR35 Series
note: a bare 'Kodak VR35' names the line; route it to the family record rather than leaving it unmatched.

name: Kodak EasyLoad 35 KE60
note: sellers drop the '35' from the line name; KE-numbers are unique within Kodak.

name: Yashica 107 MP
note: MP is the abbreviation of 'Multi Program', spelled out on the body's badge.

name: Konica FP-1
note: the 1981 FP-1's full marketing name is 'FP-1 program' (program-only exposure); one camera, one record.

name: Aires 35-III C
note: spacing twin of the 35-IIIC (1958); the spaced record is a stub with an empty lens object, the glued one carries the real spec sheet.

name: Aires 35-IIIC
note: sellers drop the '35' line number; IIIC is unique within Aires.

name: Kiev 60 TTL
note: the body is one camera sold with or without the TTL metering prism; 'Kiev 60' listings are this record.

name: Sony Mavica FD88
note: Sony's model code for every floppy Mavica is MVC-FD##, printed on the face of the camera; sellers use it interchangeably with the marketing name.

name: Praktica LLC
note: Hanimex distributed Prakticas in Commonwealth markets under its own badge; the LLC is the same Pentacon body. (Canonical direction flipped by the 2026-07 Pentacon push: bare name is now the record, the maker-prefixed duplicate folds in via 2026-07-pentacon-dedup.jsonl.)

name: Argus STL 1000
note: built by Cosina for Argus; sellers title both names, often with the slash.

name: Belca Belfoca
note: 'Belca-Werk' is the VEB factory name sellers copy off the lens rim; the record uses the short brand.

name: Rollei Rolleiflex 3,5 Automat MX (K4A)
note: US sellers name the Automat generations without the 3,5 aperture prefix the German naming carries.

name: Rollei Rolleiflex 3,5 Automat MX-EVS (K4B)
note: as above.

name: Vivitar IC 101 Panorama
note: glued spelling as printed on the shell; the 'Panorama' suffix is on the faceplate but dropped in most listings.

name: Premier Instrument Kardon
note: the company name appears with and without the plural s in period sources; 'Kardon' alone is unambiguous.

name: Ihagee Kine Exakta II
note: the 1949 body is the Kine Exakta II; sellers drop 'Kine'.

name: Minolta 16 P
note: the box says 'Minolta-16 model P'; the record name drops the hyphen and the word 'model'.

name: Sony α NEX-7
note: brand-glyph duplicate — α and Alpha are one word; the records differ only in the spelling of it.

name: Sony α NEX-5
note: as above.

name: Sony NEX-6
note: brand-word duplicate of the Alpha-prefixed record; NEX-6 is the same body.

name: Olympus Pen E-P1
note: interchangeable Micro Four Thirds body; the fixed_lens object was corpus junk (kit-lens detail filed as a fixed lens) and pairs contradictorily with lens_mount.

name: Olympus OM-D E-M5
note: as above — MFT body, kit-lens junk in fixed_lens.

name: Panasonic Lumix DMC-G1
note: as above.

name: Panasonic Lumix DMC-GH3
note: as above.

name: Panasonic Lumix DMC-G2
note: MFT mirrorless (2010); the corpus carried medium 'film', which now contradicts the sensor facts.

name: Panasonic Lumix DMC-GH1
note: as above (2009).

name: Canon Digital Ixus 60
note: 2006 digital compact; medium said 'film'. Pre-existing defect surfaced by the gate's film_with_sensor_facts check.

name: Canon Powershot A480
note: 2009 digital compact; medium said 'film'. As above.

name: QRS Devry Corp Kamra
note: one 1928 camera: QRS Co. merged with DeVry in 1929 and resold the same body; camera-wiki treats the DeVry name as a redirect to the QRS Kamra article.

name: QRS Kamra
aliases: De Vry Still Camera Model K-1
note: post-merger commercial names for the same camera.

name: Chrislin Insta-Camera Model 100
note: sellers drop the model number; Chrislin made one camera.

name: Samsung AF Zoom 777i
note: one camera under two regional names — collectiblend files it as 'Maxima Zoom 77i (AF Zoom 777i)'; Maxima is Samsung's North-American branding.

name: Fujifilm Clear Shot Plus
note: camera-wiki: 'in some countries, it appears to have been called the Smart Shot Deluxe.' No 'Deluxe II' is documented anywhere — deliberately not added.

name: Olympus AF-10 Mini
note: Infinity Hi-Lite is the US market name of the AF-10 Mini (1995).

name: Olympus AFL Quick Flash
note: the 1983 AFL — 'Quick Flash' is its tagline, 'Picasso' its Japanese nickname per camera-wiki.

name: Canon Snappy 50
note: word-order variant sellers type; the Snappy line is always 'Snappy [number]'.

name: Canon Z60 IX
note: three market names for the 1997 APS compact: ELPH 260Z (Americas), Z60 IX (Europe), IXY 25 (Japan) — camera-wiki Z60 IX / IXUS APS pages.

name: Minolta Freedom Dual Quartz Date
note: the 1987 AF-DL sold as Freedom DL / Freedom Dual in the US; the record carries the date-back suffix, sellers usually do not.

name: Olympus Camedia C-740 Ultra Zoom
note: bare designation and the UZ abbreviation, both commoner in listings than the expanded record name.

name: Sony DSC-F717
note: line-name duplicate — same 2002 bridge camera with and without the Cyber-shot prefix.

name: Sony DSC-F828
note: as above (2003).

name: Yashica T5
note: one camera, two market names — T4 Super in the US, T5 in Europe, T Proof in Japan (camera-wiki Yashica T4). The records differ only by market.

name: Yashica T4 Super
note: the European and Japanese names of the T4 Super.

name: Yashica T3
note: T Scope is the Japanese name of the T3 (camera-wiki Yashica T3).

name: Yashica T4
note: Slim T is the Japanese name of the T4.

name: Bronica SQ-A
note: Seiko #0 leaf shutters in the SQ lenses, 8s-1/500 plus T; one 6V PX28A in the body base; no built-in meter (metering only via accessory prism finders). camera-wiki Bronica SQ.

name: Mamiya M645 1000S
note: moving-coil electronic focal-plane shutter, cloth vertical-travel, B to 1/1000; one 6V PX28. camera-wiki Mamiya M645.

name: Pentax PC35 AF-M
note: the -M adds the built-in winder over the base PC35AF; programmed AE; DX reading to ISO 1600. 2x AA per Wikipedia's explicit base-vs-M split (camera-wiki's page conflates the variants and says AAA — the AA figure also matches the winder's current draw).

name: Horizont
note: KMZ, 1967-1973, 24x58mm swing-lens panoramic; sellers title it with the factory name and the word panoramic.

name: Pentax PC35 AF-M
note: the body is engraved PC35AF-M with no space; sellers glue it fully. The record's spaced 'AF-M' tokenizes differently from every glued spelling.

name: Pentax PC35 AF-M SE
note: as above, date-back variant.

name: Pentax PC35 AF
note: as above, base model.
